setup.goal: Predict which loan applicants will default, at application time.

findings.title: Possible target leakage in 'collections_flag'
findings.what: Using only 'collections_flag', a simple train-only rule reaches 96.3% normalized balanced-accuracy skill (0% = chance-level balanced accuracy, 100% = perfect) when predicting 'default'.
findings.why: A feature this strong can contain information that becomes available only after the outcome is known. It can also be a valid measurement, so the score alone does not prove leakage.
findings.fix: Check what 'collections_flag' means and when it becomes available. Remove it and retrain only if it is unavailable at prediction time or is derived from the outcome.

findings.title: Preprocessing (StandardScaler) runs before the evaluation split
findings.what: In the training code, StandardScaler is fitted on line(s) 22, before the first train/test split or cross-validation run on line 24.
findings.why: A learned step that runs before the evaluation boundary can use information from rows that later act as validation or test data. Scaling or imputation usually has a smaller effect, but the evaluation is still no longer fully independent.
findings.fix: Create the split first. Fit learned preprocessing on training data only, and keep fold-specific preprocessing inside the cross-validation Pipeline.

findings.title: The data has a full-dataset scaling fingerprint
findings.what: 6 numeric column(s) are almost perfectly standard-scaled only when training and test rows are combined.
findings.why: This pattern strongly suggests that scaling is fitted before the split. It is a fingerprint rather than direct proof, so the original data preparation should be checked.
findings.fix: Return to the raw, unscaled data. Split it first, fit the scaler on training rows only, transform the test rows with that fitted scaler, and retrain the model.

findings.title: Accuracy alone can hide poor rare-class performance
findings.what: The model is judged by accuracy from the stated reported metric: 98.9%. The minority class '1' makes up 13.0% of training rows, while an always-majority prediction already scores 85.8% on this test set. The model recalls 97.2% of the '1' test cases.
findings.why: With imbalanced classes, accuracy can stay high even when the model performs poorly on the rare class. Using accuracy alone can therefore hide behaviour that matters for the prediction goal.
findings.fix: Report recall, precision and F1 for '1', and include PR AUC when probability scores are available. Compare accuracy with the always-majority baseline instead of using it alone.

checks.name: Model runs on the data
checks.description: Checks that the model can make predictions on the provided data.

checks.name: Missing values handled differently in train and test
checks.description: Compares missing-value rates per column between training and test data.

checks.name: Missing values disguised as numbers
checks.description: Finds placeholder codes such as -999 or 9999 that can stand in for unknown values.

checks.name: New categories that only appear in test data
checks.description: Lists text categories in the test data that do not appear in the training data.

checks.name: Category codes that mean different things in train and test
checks.description: Checks whether number-coded categories behave differently between training and test data and whether a remapping explains the difference.
checks.note: The data has no number-coded category columns.

checks.name: Test data looks different from training data
checks.description: Measures numeric distribution shift between training and test data with PSI.

checks.name: Columns that give away the answer
checks.description: Tests every feature on its own. A feature with unusually high test skill can be a target proxy and needs a timing or meaning check.

checks.name: Preprocessing that learns from the test data
checks.description: Checks whether fitted preprocessing statistics match train + test data instead of training data only, and checks for full-data scaling fingerprints.

checks.name: Leaky steps in the training code
checks.description: Reads the training script or notebook without running it and flags preprocessing fitted before evaluation, fitted on test data, or whole-dataset imputation.

checks.name: Training on the future (time leakage)
checks.description: Checks whether training and test periods overlap when time order matters.
checks.note: The data has no date/time column.

checks.name: ID columns used as features
checks.description: Flags likely row or entity identifiers that the model uses as features.

checks.name: Same rows in training and test data
checks.description: Looks for test feature rows that also appear in the training data.

checks.name: Same people/entities in training and test data
checks.description: Checks whether repeated customer, patient, device, or other group values appear on both sides of a split.
checks.note: The data has no repeated group or ID column to compare.

checks.name: Cross-validation that ignores groups or time
checks.description: Reads the training code and checks whether validation respects repeated groups or time order when those structures matter.
checks.note: The audit has no confirmed group or time structure that requires special validation.

checks.name: Accuracy hiding poor results on rare cases
checks.description: On imbalanced classification data, checks whether accuracy is used as the main reported metric and compares it with rare-class performance.

checks.name: Much better on training data than on test data
checks.description: Compares the model's primary score on training and test data.

checks.name: Suspiciously perfect test score
checks.description: Flags near-perfect test scores that deserve a leakage or contamination review.

checks.name: Model ignores the rare class
checks.description: Checks whether the model collapses toward the most common class or misses whole classes.

checks.name: Imbalanced data with no counter-measure
checks.description: When one training class is rare, checks whether the model or training code uses class weighting, resampling, or sample weights.
checks.note: Smallest class is 13.0% of the training data; this check treats that as outside severe imbalance.
